jobs.title: Process Operator Specialist, Air Separation Unit (Starship) - Night Shift
jobs.description_text: PROCESS OPERATOR SPECIALIST, AIR SEPARATION UNIT (STARSHIP) - NIGHT SHIFT SpaceX is building its first production-scale Air Separation Unit (ASU) at Starbase to produce the high-purity liquid oxygen that powers Starship. This is not just another industrial plant—it is the critical on-site propellant factory that eliminates supply risk for the most ambitious launch vehicle ever built and lays the operational foundation for producing propellants on the Moon and Mars. As a process operator specialist on the ASU team, you will operate and support cryogenic distillation, turboexpanders, centrifugal compressors, molecular sieve systems, and high-purity LOX production under the direction of Lead and Level 4/5 operators. You will monitor process parameters, execute approved procedures, complete thorough field rounds, and qualify toward independent watch standing. If you thrive in high-stakes cryogenic environments, want to learn these systems from first principles, and want ownership of mission-critical hardware as you grow, this is the role for you. RESPONSIBILITIES: Monitor the ASU via distributed control system/human-machine interface and conduct thorough field rounds, identifying equipment and process deviations early and reporting them immediately Execute assigned steps of plant startups, shutdowns, mode changes, and abnormal situation response in accordance with approved operating procedures and alarm response matrices Support troubleshooting, maintenance, and calibration of AS

This is a special opportunity to work at the cutting edge of satellite technologies with a world-class team focused on connecting the unconnected. jobs.description_text: PROPULSION ENGINEER, RAPTOR INTEGRATION The Raptor Fleet Operations team is responsible for the fleet of Raptor Engines from the time they leave the factory in Hawthorne until the time they fly. Today, the team is focused on enabling rapid design iteration by taking lessons from flight and engine testing and applying those lessons across the fleet. In the future, the team will begin to focus on developing the processes necessary to maintain a large fleet of engines capable of continuous reuse. As a Propulsion Engineer on this team, you will serve an important role in developing the processes that will be used to maintain the fleet of engines and will be the technical interface between the hardware and RE teams. Engineers in this role demonstrate a very high level of engineering intuition, critical thinking, system level expertise, and are comfortable working under tight deadlines with loosely defined requirements and minimal oversight. Combining these skills, these engineers face challenges across a wide variety of work centers at the company and are at the forefront of developing integration and test processes for current and next generation engines. jobs.description_text: PROPULSION ENGINEER, STAGE SYSTEMS (STARSHIP) The Stage Responsible Engineer (Stage RE) develops the fluid systems required to enable higher-performance, highly manufacturable interplanetary vehicles. This role develops the design, operation, and performance of the stage propulsion systems on the Starship launch vehicle. The stage propulsion systems include all propellant feed systems, propellant management systems, helium pressurization systems, pneumatic systems, autogenous pressurization systems, differential pressure measurement systems, engine ignition gas supply systems, environmental control systems, and attitude control systems integrated into each stage of the vehicle. The Stage RE owns overall stage propulsion system performance for each vehicle and mission. jobs.title: Propulsion Software Engineer (Falcon Engineering)
jobs.description_text: PROPULSION SOFTWARE ENGINEER (FALCON ENGINEERING) The Falcon Engineering team is dedicated to delivering Falcon and its payloads to orbit rapidly and reliably. As a Propulsion Software Engineer, you enable the long-term success of Falcon and its Merlin engines, improve hardware reliability, and remove recurring, time-consuming work from engineers’ plates so they can focus on hard engineering. You do this by building agentic AI systems, MCP servers, RAG-based search, and traditional automation where it is the right solution. You own problems end-to-end: scoping the solution with the engineers who have the problem, rolling it out, measuring the time it saves, and maintaining it as the vehicle and processes evolve. We are looking for engineers with hands-on hardware experience (engine test, fluid systems, or structures) who can code, so that the tools they build reflect how the hardware actually behaves and fails. Using that background, you will also support root cause analysis for anomaly resolution, providing data and model-driven insights to help operations and hardware teams with high-consequence decision making. With hundreds of Falcon launches and thousands of engine test operations, the work we do impacts both the hardware design process and the operation of every single mission and engine test. jobs.title: PVD Equipment Engineer, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jobs.description_text: PVD EQUIPMENT ENGINEER, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK) Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that is capable of delivering high-speed internet to even the most remote locations. As a Solar Cell PVD Equipment Engineer, you will own the PVD (Physical Vapor Deposition / sputtering) equipment used to manufacture silicon heterojunction solar cells at massive scale. You will work closely with our existing PVD Process Engineering team to ensure world-class equipment performance, reliability, and uptime. While the process team focuses on film properties (e.g., TCO layers), sheet resistance, and cell efficiency, you will be the hardware owner responsible for tool availability, stability, and scaling to support our ambitious goals. Your work will form the backbone of the Starlink network (photons of sunlight in is directly proportional to photons of data out to customers!) and help provide internet to tens of millions of customers all around the world. You will spearhead state of the art production equipment for an internal solar cell production line, providing high efficiency and high-quality solar cells for both our latest generation Starlink satellites and for Starship missions to the Moon and Mars. jobs.description_text: SERVER HARDWARE SYSTEMS ENGINEER (STARLINK) Starlink delivers high-speed, low-latency internet to millions of people around the world, and the network depends on a global fleet of servers running in data centers and points of presence (PoPs). The Starlink Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team is hiring a Server Hardware Systems Engineer to own the health of this fleet as it scales rapidly. You will own the server hardware lifecycle from issue detection, to repair, through recovery. You will build the telemetry, alerting, and automation that let a small team operate a very large fleet, and coordinate with network operations, field technicians, hardware vendors, and data center partners to get failed hardware repaired and back into service quickly. You will also use fleet reliability data to shape server design, selection, and qualification for new sites across both commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) and custom-designed server platforms. The right engineer for this job is one who is automation-first. Our goal is to scale operations for server hardware through excellent tooling, and automated process. jobs.title: Sr. Fluids Systems Engineer, Production (Starship)
jobs.description_text: SR. FLUIDS ENGINEER, PRODUCTION (STARSHIP) Starship is the largest and most capable space launch system ever developed. With the capability to deliver in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit, it will fundamentally change access to space, and is the technology that will be used to establish a self-sustaining city on Mars. We will ultimately need thousands of Starships to accomplish that feat. The Starbase production fluids team builds, maintains, and operates the fluid systems the Starship factory runs on. This includes high pressure production test equipment used to validate vehicles and components, vehicle press systems, and cleaning and contamination control equipment. Engineers on this team own hardware from problem statement through design, build, commissioning, and handoff to the technicians and operators who use it every day. We are looking for hands-on engineers who can reduce a messy production problem to first principles, design the simplest system that meets the requirement, and stay with it until it is fully handed off and documented. You will work directly with our build shop, partner teams, and production customers on an accelerated schedule. RESPONSIBILITIES: Design, build, and commission fluid systems for Starship production, including test systems, manufacturing systems, and cleaning equipment. jobs.description_text: SR. FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe. As a Sr. Full Stack Engineer, you will work closely with a mix of both external customers and internal partners across all engineering disciplines here at SpaceX to bring observability to a rapidly expanding network of millions of assets. The tools and applications you build will empower Starlink customers to manage their deployed assets in aviation, maritime, and enterprise environments while also bringing enhanced development to key features across various internal and external platforms. On this team, we will rely on you to be a key figure in the successful development of mission critical, high performance web applications. jobs.title: Technical Buyer
jobs.description_text: The Vehicle team builds the aircraft at the heart of Rainmaker’s cloud seeding operations. We design, build, and fly autonomous drones that go where other systems won’t. Our aircraft fly into icing, turbulence, high winds, and low visibility, because that’s where the clouds worth seeding are. We own the full flight system end to end: UAS: airframe, propulsion, avionics, and the autonomy that keeps our aircraft flying safely and reliably in severe weather. Dispersion payload: the hardware that delivers seeding material precisely, at the right place and time inside a cloud. Sensing systems: onboard instruments that measure the atmosphere around the aircraft, so we can see conditions as they happen and show what each mission accomplished. We’re a small, hands-on team that takes hardware from first sketch to field deployment. Engineers here design a part, test it on the bench, and watch it fly in conditions most drone programs would ground for. If you like hard problems where the environment fights back, and you want your work to put water on the ground, you’ll fit in here.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter
jobs.description_text: We are hiring a Technical Recruiter to help build Rainmaker's technical recruiting engine: the system that hires exceptional technical, scientific, and operational talent with an extraordinary bar of excellence. You will own recruiting end to end: how we source, how we run interviews, how we make decisions, and how candidates experience Rainmaker from first contact to signed offer. You will partner closely with the Head of People, leadership, and hiring managers, but recruiting execution is yours.

jobs.title: Vehicle Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: The vehicle software team builds the software that operates Rainmaker’s cloud-seeding vehicles, connecting flight control, onboard computing, sensors, payloads, and ground operations. We work closely with electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and flight operations teams to turn new hardware into reliable systems that can be built, deployed, and operated at scale. Our goal is to make every vehicle a dependable tool for delivering more freshwater where it is needed.

jobs.title: FP&A Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role As our FP&A Intern, you’ll work on the numbers leadership uses to run the company. You’ll help build the annual plan, quarterly forecasts, and long-range models, and you’ll present your work to our senior leadership team. You’ll report to the FP&A Manager and work on the real plan, the real forecasts, and the materials that go in front of our board. Neighbor is a two-sided marketplace, which makes the finance work here unusually interesting. You’ll dig into how supply and demand grow market by market, what drives our take rate, and what it costs to acquire a host or a renter. By the end of the summer, you’ll own expense forecasting for the entire business. This internship is a direct path to a full-time role. Strong performers leave with a full-time offer to join the team after graduation.

jobs.title: Head of Performance Marketing
jobs.description_text: At Neighbor, we're building the largest hyperlocal storage and parking marketplace in the world. We've raised over $75 million from top-tier investors including Andreessen Horowitz and the CEOs of DoorDash, StockX, and Uber. Our marketplace operates in all 50 states, and we're just getting started.

jobs.title: Marketplace Growth Associate
jobs.description_text: About the Role As a Marketplace Growth Associate, you’ll work with Neighbor’s hosts: the commercial and residential property owners who list their storage and parking space on our marketplace. Hosts are the supply side of everything we do. The more easily renters can find a host’s space, the more that host earns and the faster the marketplace grows in every city we serve. You’ll be one of the people making that happen, one host at a time. Most of your day (50–75%) is outbound phone calls with hosts. On each call, you’ll help a host make their listing stronger and easier to find: setting up a Google Maps pin, tightening photos and descriptions, getting the price right, and building up reviews. The goal is to turn their space into steady, growing income. The rest of your time is operations: running the signage program, tracking results and finding ways to make the whole thing work better. This role fits you if you like being on the phone, you can manage a high volume of work on your own, and you tend to notice when a process could run better.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description_text: At Neighbor, we’re building the largest hyperlocal marketplace the world has ever seen. We’ve raised over $75 million from top-tier investors such as Andreessen Horowitz and the CEOs of DoorDash, StockX, and Uber. Our marketplace is already flourishing in all 50 states and we’re just getting started! As a Product Manager, you will be responsible for setting the vision, defining the strategy, and driving the execution of a meaningful part of our marketplace. You will pioneer a standard of customer obsession, analytical rigor, and AI-augmented velocity that makes Neighbor fundamentally better for our hosts and renters across all 50 states.

jobs.title: UX Designer (Junior, Mid and Senior Level Opportunities Available)
jobs.description_text: About the Role Neighbor is a two-sided marketplace for self storage and vehicle storage. Hosts list everything from garages and driveways to RV pads and commercial facility units, and renters compare options, book, and manage reservations through Neighbor’s website and apps. You’ll report directly to a Co-Founder and our VP of Product & Design, and you’ll set the bar for design craft across the company. That means mentoring Neighbor’s other designers, shaping product direction with PMs and engineers from the first sketch, and making sure real renter insight reaches every team. Renters on Neighbor compare everything from storage facility units to neighborhood garages and RV pads. Helping them choose with confidence is a hard design problem, and solving it moves the business directly. This role is based in our Lehi, Utah office, in person Tuesday through Friday, with the option to work from home on Mondays.

jobs.title: 3D Computer Vision Researcher – Remote (US)
jobs.location_raw: Remote, USA: AL, AZ, CO, DC, FL, GA, IL, IN, MA, MD, ME, MN, NC, NJ, NM, NY, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, UT, VA, WI
jobs.description_text: Advance 3D Vision Research from Algorithms to Open Source Applications. In this position, you’ll research and develop algorithms for photogrammetry, camera calibration, registration, and 3D reconstruction from images and video. Current projects emphasize aerial and satellite imagery, with opportunities to adapt these capabilities to new challenges and data domains such as underwater imagery and synthetic aperture radar. Your work will contribute to open source applications and frameworks including TeleSculptor, KWIVER, and Danesfield. You’ll also explore how 3D vision can support broader computer vision problems such as object detection and tracking, change detection, super resolution, and video compression. Kitware partners with government R&D agencies, branches of the U.S. military, members of the Intelligence Community, and commercial organizations ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies. You’ll have opportunities to collaborate directly with customers, participate in field tests and demonstrations, publish novel work, and apply state-of-the-art artificial intelligence approaches to real-world national security challenges.

jobs.description_text: Company at a Glance OpenX is focused on unleashing the full economic potential of digital media companies. We do this by making digital advertising markets and technologies that are designed to deliver optimal value to publishers and advertisers on every ad served across all screens. At OpenX, we have built a team that is uniquely experienced in designing and operating high-scale ad marketplaces, and we are constantly on the lookout for thoughtful, creative executors who are as fascinated as we are about finding new ways to apply a blend of market design, technical innovation, operational excellence, and empathetic partner service to the frontiers of digital advertising. jobs.title: Sr Director, DSP Partnerships & Growth
jobs.description_text: OpenX is seeking a strategic, commercially driven Senior Director, DSP Partnerships & Growth (Americas) to lead the regional DSP partnerships organization and accelerate revenue growth across established and emerging buying platforms. As the programmatic ecosystem evolves, OpenX is redefining how supply-side and demand-side platforms collaborate to drive performance, efficiency, and innovation. This leader will play a critical role in strengthening our position with leading DSPs, expanding demand diversification, and translating emerging market opportunities into sustainable commercial growth. This is more than a traditional partnership management role. We're looking for a commercial builder and strategic operator who can independently lead a high-performing team, establish executive-level relationships, identify new growth opportunities, and turn complex technical capabilities into differentiated business value. Reporting to the Global Head of DSP, this leader will drive the commercial growth and execution of OpenX's US DSP partnerships, translating strategic priorities into measurable revenue outcomes while collaborating closely with DSP Operations, Product, and cross-functional commercial teams.

jobs.title: SVP, Global Buyer Development
jobs.description_text: OpenX is seeking a dynamic and experienced Senior Vice President of Global Buyer Development to lead our agency and brand facing Sales and Account Management teams. This executive will be responsible for driving global buyer strategy, growing revenue, and owning customer relationships across agency holding companies, independent agencies, and direct brands. This person will be a member of the OpenX Leadership Team. As a senior leader within the organization, the Senior Vice President will play a critical role in shaping the future of OpenX’s buyer development business. The ideal candidate will possess deep preexisting buyer relationships, understanding of programmatic advertising, a strategic mindset for business development and customer service, and a proven ability to build and lead high performing teams. This person will maintain executive relationships with leading agencies and brands, serve as a market representative of OpenX, and identify opportunities that shape our value proposition and market position. The Senior Vice President will collaborate closely with leadership across Publisher Development, DSP Partnerships, Partnerships, Product, Marketing, Commercial Operations, Finance, Legal, and HR. This person will report directly to the EVP, Commercial.

jobs.title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
jobs.description_text: The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.

The ideal candidate enjoys working at the intersection of data engineering and business operations. You will be expected to understand how recruiting workflows generate data and build practical solutions that improve day to day operations. This role is well suited for someone who can move fluidly between building a pipeline, debugging an integration, creating a dashboard, documenting an operating procedure, and helping stakeholders understand how to use the resulting tool.

jobs.title: GNC Engineer - Controls
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a GNC Engineer II who focuses on flight controls to evaluate and tune our existing control laws, so the aircraft has stable, responsive, and predictable handling across the flight envelope. You will use CONDUIT and our existing simulation environment to analyze the control laws against stability and performance criteria, tune their gains, and check their behavior in Monte Carlo and full-mission simulations before they go to flight test. You will work closely with the GNC engineers who own the control law architecture, as well as the firmware, aeromechanical, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a solid grounding in linear control theory and aircraft flight dynamics, and enjoys the analytical work of understanding why a control system behaves the way it does and how to improve it. Experience with frequency-domain control system analysis is highly desirable.

jobs.title: GNC Engineer - Navigation
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a GNC Engineer II who focuses on navigation to design, implement, and verify the state estimation and sensor fusion algorithms. These algorithms estimate the aircraft’s attitude, heading, position, velocity, and other critical states in real time. You will work across the full development lifecycle. That includes characterizing sensors and designing algorithms in MATLAB and Simulink, deploying them on embedded flight hardware, testing them in simulation and hardware-in-the-loop, and analyzing flight test data. You will work closely with the flight controls, firmware, avionics, autonomy, systems engineering, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a solid grounding in estimation theory and hands-on experience taking a filter from design all the way to real sensor data or hardware. Experience with aircraft navigation systems, GNSS/INS integration, and eVTOL or UAV platforms is highly desirable.

jobs.title: Senior GNC Engineer - Flight Controls
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a Senior GNC Engineer to design, tune, and verify flight control laws for our aircraft, taking them from analysis and simulation through flight test. You will own the control laws for specific flight modes and control loops within the architecture set by the team’s technical leads. That includes analysis and tuning with CONDUIT, system identification to support our models, Monte Carlo and mission-level verification, and flight test support. You will work closely with the navigation, firmware, aeromechanical, systems engineering, and flight test teams, and help mentor less experienced engineers. The ideal candidate is a fully qualified flight controls engineer who works independently, has designed and tuned control laws that were evaluated in flight test or piloted simulation, ideally on VTOL, rotorcraft, or eVTOL aircraft, and brings sound judgment to interpreting analysis and test results.

jobs.title: Staff GNC Engineer – Flight Controls
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a Staff GNC Engineer to lead flight control law development on an aircraft program: owning the control law architecture and its design, tuning, and verification from simulation through flight test. You will set the technical direction for how our aircraft are controlled in hover, transition, and forward flight. That includes defining the control law architecture and design criteria, using system identification and flight data to improve our models, and making sure the control laws meet stability, performance, and handling qualities requirements. You will also be a team lead for flight controls, setting priorities for the team, overseeing its technical work, and mentoring the engineers on it, while working closely with the navigation, firmware, aeromechanical, systems engineering, safety, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a track record of taking flight control laws from design to flight on real aircraft, ideally VTOL, rotorcraft, or eVTOL, and the judgment to make sound design and flight test decisions with incomplete information. This role is a strong next step for an engineer who has grown through hands-on flight controls work and is ready to lead a team.

The role will support core accounting activities, including general ledger maintenance, account reconciliations, and month-end close, while providing supplemental support to tax, reporting and FP&A teams as needed. The Staff Accountant will also coordinate with the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions of Fenway Sports Group’s affiliated entities to ensure accurate financial records and timely processing of intercompany transactions. The base salary range for this position is $60,000-$70,000 based on relevant experience. Additionally, this position qualifies for annual incentive pay along with our comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: IT Project Manager Assistant
jobs.description_text: DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW: The Information Technology department provides strategic direction and day-to-day IT operational, software and emerging technology support for the Red Sox, Fenway Sports Management, the Red Sox Foundation, and FSG Real Estate. Responsibilities include support for corporate and ballpark infrastructure, systems architecture, networks, computer and auxiliary operations, desktop support, data and cyber security, and broadcast cabling and related infrastructure. Provides applications development and support for corporate systems, MLB Ballpark and fan engagement apps, and systems and data architecture. POSITION OVERVIEW: The Information Technology department is seeking a part-time IT Project Manager Assistant to support the Project Management Organization (PMO) and ensure the accuracy and consistency of our data across multiple Business systems. This role will assist in project management: gathering requirements, documenting processes, and coordinating with both stakeholders and developers in an Agile environment to help solve business problems and inefficiencies with technology. The role will also be responsible for IT onboarding and offboarding: creating and maintaining user accounts across downstream systems and identifying and resolving discrepancies. The hourly rate for this position is $28.

jobs.title: Minor League Complex Hitting Analyst and Rehab Coach
jobs.description_text: DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW: The Player Development department is dedicated to fostering the comprehensive growth of our minor league players. Our mission is to excel in optimizing talent and skill development while aligning with player and team objectives. Our approach involves the creation of world class player programs and efficiently scaling them across our player pool. Collaborating closely with baseball analytics, performance, and medical, we establish effective frameworks for experimentation and learning. Additionally, we work closely with Amateur Scouting, International Scouting, and Pro Scouting to ensure seamless player transitions into the Red Sox organization. POSITION OVERVIEW: The Complex Hitting Analyst & Rehab Coach will work closely with the Hitting Coordinator, Complex Hitting Coaches, and necessary auxiliary staff to support the daily needs of the hitting department. The role will be primarily responsible for building reports and tools using Snowflake and other available data sources, while also assisting with the daily execution of rehab hitting activities at the complex. As the Red Sox continue to build a team capable of being THE standard in player AND Staff development, we are looking for candidates who are organized, humble, proactive, and capable of communicating effectively across departments and levels of the organization. The position is based out of the Player Development Complex in Fort Myers, FL. This position is seasonal, with full-time consideration f

jobs.title: Senior Coordinator, Youth Baseball and Softball
jobs.description_text: DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW: The Red Sox Foundation is one of the largest team charities in Major League Baseball, strategically using its platform to be a leading source of hope and positivity off the field in the areas of health, education and recreation. By coupling our year-round, direct-service programming with our grant-making initiatives and core partnerships, we utilize a unique model as a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization to effectively triple our impact in New England and Lee County, Florida. It is the passion of the best fans in baseball that make our work possible. POSITION OVERVIEW: The Senior Coordinator, Youth Baseball and Softball will be a significant contributor to the Programs Team to coordinate and effectively deliver the Red Sox Foundation’s year-round direct service youth baseball and softball programming with the goal of Growing the Game. The base salary range for this position is $55,000-$60,000 based on proven relevant experience. Additionally, this position qualifies for annual incentive pay along with a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Sr. Developer, Baseball Systems
jobs.description_text: DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW: Members of the Baseball Systems team at the Boston Red Sox are focused on designing, building, and refining the software and data pipelines used within Baseball Operations. These tools and applications are an integral part of the decision-making process, are directly integrated in the workflows of all departments within Baseball Operations, and provide an efficient, consistent, and accessible experience when interacting with our internal data sources and applications. POSITION OVERVIE W: The Sr Developer, Baseball Systems position will be a member of the baseball operations software development team, and is responsible for the design, development, and support, of all baseball systems. This individual will work closely with members of baseball operations to understand business requirements that drive the analysis, design, and development of quality baseball systems and solutions. This position is responsible for designing and building highly complex front end applications and will collaborate closely with colleagues on the software development team and baseball operations personnel from all departments. The base salary range for this position is $110,000-$130,000 based on proven relevant experience. Additionally, this position qualifies for annual incentive pay along with a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Art Director
jobs.description_text: About the Role: We’re looking for a versatile Art Director to support our creative team on a contract basis, working approximately two days per week. You will be responsible for defining visual and tonal guidelines, shaping storytelling strategies, and conceptualizing engaging brand content across PR and editorial channels, while also helping the executive leadership team with key assets. This person will take projects through final delivery, operating as both a high-level strategist and a hands-on creator to ensure all output beautifully delivers against both performance and brand objectives while maintaining a consistent visual standard. Contract Details Schedule: 16 hours/week, Monday–Friday Contract Duration: 3-6 months

jobs.title: Avionics Electrical Engineer
jobs.description_text: About The Role: As an Avionics Electrical Engineer at Hermeus, you will be responsible for the design, testing, and integration of GNC systems, electrical hardware, control software, power distribution, and RF communications for our hypersonic vehicles. Avionics Electrical Engineer I $91,800-$112,200 Avionics Electrical Engineer II $114,750-$140,250 Senior Avionics Electrical Engineer $138,550-$187,450 This position is open to multiple experience levels. The final job level and compensation package will be determined during the interview process based on the candidate's experience, technical depth, scope of ownership, and demonstrated ability to operate at the appropriate level. Candidates are encouraged to apply even if their experience does not align perfectly with every qualification listed above.

jobs.title: Build Engineer
jobs.description_text: Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. About The Role: This role sits at the intersection of engineering design, manufacturing, integration and test for flight vehicles. You'll be embedded with design and production teams, owning everything from hardware design, tooling, testing and flight readiness to process development and vehicle assembly. Build Engineer I $91,800 - 112,200 Build Engineer II $114,750 - $140,250

jobs.title: Business Development Analyst
jobs.description_text: About the Role: The Business Development team at Hermeus is seeking a dynamic and innovative professional to expand our engagement with the defense and aviation enterprise. We are looking for a high-performer—someone who embraces challenges and consistently adds value in a fast-paced environment. We seek someone who can effectively represent our company’s vision to critical stakeholders, identify and pursue opportunities to enhance our government and national security efforts, while collaborating seamlessly with our engineering, operations, and product teams as we build the world’s fastest aircraft. We’re adding to our team with one overarching goal: advancing government partnerships to accelerate the development and deployment of autonomous aircraft. Come join us and build a public-private partnership that will lead to a faster future.

jobs.title: Chief Engineer - Airbreathing Propulsion Test
jobs.description_text: About The Role: Hermeus is seeking a hands-on, technically rigorous Chief Engineer to lead the expansion of our High Enthalpy Airbreathing Test (HEAT) facility in Jacksonville, Florida. This is a high-ownership role for an engineer who has built, integrated, commissioned, and operated complex propulsion test infrastructure—and is ready to lead the next phase of capability development. You will own the technical execution of the facility expansion from requirements definition and architecture through design, construction, system integration, commissioning, and operational readiness. Working across propulsion engineering, test operations, facilities, contractors, and government stakeholders, you will translate demanding propulsion test objectives into safe, reliable, high-performance test capabilities. This is not simply a facilities project management role. We are looking for an engineer who understands how propulsion test systems work, can make sound technical decisions across interconnected systems, and can drive execution from concept to first operation. You will serve as the technical authority for the expansion, balancing test capability, safety, schedule, cost, and future scalability. Based on Hermeus’ rapid hardware development philosophy, you will have the opportunity to build test infrastructure that directly accelerates the development of advanced airbreathing propulsion systems.

jobs.title: Flight Software Engineer – Command & Control
jobs.description_text: About The Role: We are seeking a Software Engineer to join our Command & Control team in Atlanta. The team is responsible for the design, development, integration, testing, and delivery of software supporting Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), Pilot Vehicle Interfaces (PVI), Command & Control (C2), telemetry, and vehicle communications. This role will focus primarily on the embedded flight software and networking that enable communication between our aircraft and ground control systems. You will develop software supporting command and control, telemetry, network management, RF communications, and vehicle data links while working closely with avionics, RF, flight software, and ground systems engineers. This is not a traditional voice communications role. You will work on the software and network infrastructure that allow an air vehicle and ground control station to reliably exchange commands, telemetry, and other mission-critical data. The ideal candidate is comfortable moving between embedded C/C++ development, network and communications system design, and hands-on testing with target hardware. You will have ownership across both the vehicle and ground sides of the communications network and will help take systems from initial architecture through integration and flight operations.

jobs.title: Lead Technician, Propulsion & Fluids
jobs.description_text: As a Lead Technician, Propulsion & Fluids, you will oversee the build, installation, and testing of complex fluid systems, electromechanical systems, pneumatic systems, that support our flight and propulsion hardware. You’ll lead a team of technicians through the development and execution of hydraulics, pressurized systems, sub-assemblies, and mechanisms, collaborating directly with engineering and operations to deliver high-reliability builds in a fast-paced environment. This role requires deep technical fluency, strong leadership skills, and a relentless drive to improve system quality, repeatability, and performance.

jobs.title: Regulatory Compliance Counsel
jobs.description_text: About the Role: Hermeus is hiring a regulatory compliance attorney to build and run its export control and trade compliance program. You will be the go-to advisor on ITAR, EAR, and related trade controls, own jurisdiction and classification work, and prepare export authorizations. This role sits on-site alongside the engineering teams, and that placement is deliberate. You will learn Hermeus' hardware, software, and technical data well enough to make sound classification and marking calls quickly. You will also shape compliance into engineering workflows from the start. This is a hands-on builder role. You will write the policies, train the workforce, make the classification calls, and file the licenses. You will also find ways to use AI tools to speed up the work and give employees self-service answers to routine compliance questions. Depending on your background, the role can also cover advising on CUI, proprietary and technical data protection, Department of War contracting and security requirements, FCPA, anti-bribery and corruption, ethics, and FAA and FCC regulatory matters. In addition, the role may support direct and indirect supplier and consultant agreements and intellectual property matters.

jobs.description_text: About The Role: As a Senior IT Support Specialist, you will be a senior individual contributor and the hands-on technical anchor for daily IT operations. You will resolve the issues no one else can, mentor junior staff, and own the technical layer beneath the service desk: endpoint management, identity, and endpoint security. We are looking for someone who does not just close tickets but eliminates the work behind them, automating manual processes with PowerShell, replacing one-off fixes with repeatable procedures, and maturing how IT operates as we scale. You will partner closely with our Cyber, Networking, and People teams on work that crosses team boundaries. This role reports to the IT Service Desk Manager and is based on site at our Los Angeles office. Two shifts are available, 7:00am to 4:00pm or 9:00am to 6:00pm, with flexibility based on team coverage. Candidates are expected to travel to other Hermeus sites to support projects and operations.

jobs.description_text: About The Role: The Mission Systems Engineering team develops the Mission Management System—the software platform connecting mission subsystems, autonomy services, operator interfaces, communications links, and telemetry across Hermeus aircraft and ground systems. As a Senior/Principal Mission Software Engineer, you will architect, build, integrate, and validate critical portions of this platform. You will work across software, avionics, communications, autonomy, simulation, and flight operations to solve complex problems in distributed, hardware-connected environments. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with the opportunity to define foundational architecture and directly influence how Hermeus aircraft are commanded, monitored, tested, and expanded with new mission capabilities. Senior - 150,000 - 200,000 Principal - 170,00 - 230,000

jobs.title: Workplace Operations Specialist
jobs.description_text: About the Role: We're looking for a contract Workplace Operations Specialist to keep our office running smoothly day to day. You'll be the onsite point of contact for workplace needs, making sure the space is organized, stocked, and welcoming for employees and visitors. You'll work closely with Workplace Operations, Facilities, IT, Security, People, property management, and vendors to keep the workplace experience consistent. Contract Details Schedule: 25 hours/week, Monday–Friday, 9:00am–2:00pm Contract Duration: 6 months initially

jobs.title: Medical Coder - Remote
jobs.description_text: About Sprinter Health At Sprinter Health, our mission is reimagining how people access care by bringing it directly into their homes.
